patterns: APPSC asks direct dates and names: Widow Remarriage Act 1856, Female Infanticide Prevention Act 1870, Lex Loci Act 1850 (convert inherits), Ranade calling Veeresalingam 'South Indian Vidyasagar'.
Recurring traps: Widow Remarriage Act passed under Canning (not Dalhousie); 1872 Act ages 14/18; 1891 consent age 12.
Other PSCs/UPSC ask Native Marriage Act-Keshab Sen, Malabari and the Age of Consent Act (Tilak opposed), Vidyasagar's Bahuvivah and Bethune School secretaryship, Karve's women's university.
AP tilt is concentrated on Veeresalingam (girls' school, first Andhra widow remarriage 1881) and Andhra women reformers.
App MCQs add chronology and multi-statement items on age laws and western-India institutions; PYQs stay at single-fact level.
